# Green Bean

> Green Bean keeps your Slack status green (active) during your work hours — even when your computer is off. Set your work schedule once and a cloud worker holds your presence active during that window; outside it, you automatically go away.

Green Bean is an independent third-party tool and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Slack Technologies, Inc. It never reads your messages or DMs, and credentials are encrypted at rest.

## What it does
- Keeps Slack presence "active" (the green dot) automatically during configured work hours (days, time range, timezone).
- Works while your PC is off — a cloud process maintains the connection for you.
- Connect a workspace manually today; a browser extension for one-click connect is in development.
- Free plan: 1 workspace. Pro plan: up to 3 workspaces. A 14-day free trial is included.

## How to use
1. Sign in with Google.
2. Connect your Slack workspace (see the connection guide).
3. Set your work schedule (days, hours, timezone). Green Bean keeps you green in that window and turns off otherwise.

## FAQ
- Does it really show green to other people? Yes. It maintains the same kind of connection the Slack web client uses, so you appear active to others.
- Is it safe? Credentials are encrypted and messages/DMs are never read. Because it is automation, it may be subject to your workspace's policy and Slack's terms.
- Does it need admin approval? No. It works with your own web session, so no separate app install approval is required.
- Can I turn it off anytime? Yes. One toggle in the dashboard stops it immediately.
